title: Google Summer of Code (GSoC) 2026
description: Global program bringing new contributors into open source software development. Contributors work with open source organizations on a 12+ week programming project under mentor guidance.
eligibility: 18+ years old at registration; open to student developers and beginners in open source software.
stipend: $1,500 – $3,000 USD (India PPP-adjusted stipend tier)
timeline: Applications opened Mar 16, 2026; Deadline Mar 31, 2026 at 18:00 UTC; Coding May – Sept 2026
required_materials: Detailed project proposal doc, prior GitHub PRs/contributions to chosen mentoring organization, resume.
mentor_notes: GSoC 2026 contributor applications ran March 16 – March 31, 2026. Have mentees begin contributing to target org repositories between November and February ahead of the next March application window.
target_persona: Pre-final & final year CS undergrads with solid Git fundamentals and enthusiasm for Linux/C++/Python/Rust.

title: MLH Fellowship — Fall 2026 Cohort
description: Intensive 12-week remote internship alternative where fellows collaborate on production open source projects used by millions, guided by staff engineering mentors.
eligibility: 18+ years old, proficient in English, intermediate-to-advanced coding skills in at least one core language, prior participation in at least 1 MLH Hackathon or Global Hack Week.
stipend: Up to $5,000 USD educational stipend (varies by track and region)
timeline: Fall 2026 Deadline: Aug 31, 2026 (Cohort runs Sept 14 – Dec 4, 2026); Spring 2027 runs Jan – Apr 2027
required_materials: Original code sample (deployed project, no class assignments), behavioral essays, initial video interview, technical code walkthrough.
mentor_notes: The Fall 2026 batch deadline was August 31, 2026 (program runs Sept 14 – Dec 4, 2026). Applications submitted now are evaluated on a rolling basis for the Spring 2027 cohort (Jan–Apr 2027).
target_persona: Undergrads seeking tier-1 engineering experience without US visa constraints.

title: LFX Mentorship (Linux Foundation) — 2026 Fall Term
subcategory: Cloud Native, Kernel, Kubernetes & AI Infrastructure
description: Three-term annual mentorship initiative for open source developers within CNCF, Kubernetes, Linux Kernel, RISC-V, and PyTorch ecosystems with 1-on-1 maintainer guidance.
eligibility: At least 18 years old, eligible to receive stipend via LFX platform, demonstrated C/Go/Rust/Python proficiency.
stipend: $3,000 – $6,600 USD (Depending on region and project)
timeline: Mentee applications: Aug 3 – Aug 18, 2026; Fall Term runs Sept 7 – Nov 27, 2026 (Spring Term opens mid-Jan)
required_materials: LFX profile, resume, cover letter/statement of intent, and project-specific prerequisite tasks on GitHub.
mentor_notes: 2026 Fall Term mentee applications ran August 3 – August 18, 2026 (mentorship runs Sept 7 – Nov 27, 2026). Next term (Spring 2027) opens for mentee applications in February.
target_persona: Backend, DevOps, and systems programmers interested in Kubernetes, WebAssembly, and distributed systems.

title: Emergent Ventures Grant (India & Global)
description: Fast-grant fellowship supporting moonshot thinkers, researchers, and builders with bold ideas to meaningfully improve society, technology, AI, longevity, or Indian innovation.
eligibility: Open to builders, researchers, writers, and software creators of any age worldwide. Dedicated EV India cohort track available.
stipend: $5,000 – $100,000 USD equity-free grant + conference travel
timeline: Continuous year-round rolling evaluation (Decisions typically in 2–4 weeks)
required_materials: 1,500-word proposal on what you are building, why it is non-consensus, your speed of execution, and 1–2 references.
mentor_notes: Genuinely rolling year-round. Tyler Cowen and Shruti Rajagopalan (EV India) look for high agency, unusual autodidacts, and rapid prototype velocity.
target_persona: High-agency student builders working on hardware, novel AI architectures, public goods, or deep tech.

title: GitHub Campus Experts Program (2026)
description: Selective leadership program training undergraduate students to build and lead technical communities on campus, providing funding for campus events and direct GitHub mentorship.
eligibility: 18+ years old, enrolled in an accredited college/university with at least 1 year remaining before graduation, active GitHub Student Developer Pack.
stipend: Campus event sponsorship grants, travel support, GitHub swag & mentorship
timeline: Applications opened July 1, 2026; Deadline July 31, 2026 (6-week Campus Expert Training follows)
required_materials: Application form and 5-minute video introduction analyzing your local campus technical community and goals.
mentor_notes: The 2026 application window ran July 1 – July 31, 2026. Ensure 1st and 2nd year mentees activate their GitHub Student Developer Pack now so they satisfy the 6-month account tenure requirement.
target_persona: Student community organizers, hackathon leads, and open source club presidents.

title: Microsoft Learn Student Ambassadors (MLSA)
description: Global community of on-campus technology champions who mentor peers, host technical workshops using Microsoft AI & Azure tools, and advance through Alpha, Beta, and Gold milestones.
eligibility: Full-time students at least 16 years old enrolled in an accredited academic institution.
stipend: $150/mo Azure credits, free Microsoft certification vouchers, LinkedIn Learning, event support
timeline: Applications accepted year-round on a rolling basis with quarterly cohort onboarding
required_materials: Online registration, community leadership profile, and technical community contribution path.
mentor_notes: Open year-round on a rolling basis. Great foundational credential for 1st and 2nd year engineering students to gain cloud credits and workshop hosting experience.
target_persona: 1st & 2nd year undergraduate engineering students building their developer advocacy profile.

title: Outreachy Open Source Internships (Dec 2026 – Mar 2027 Cohort)
subcategory: Diversity in Open Source, Systems & Data Science

stipend: $7,000 USD total internship stipend

mentor_notes: Per outreachy.org: Initial applications for the Dec 2026 – Mar 2027 cohort opened Aug 24, 2026 and closed Aug 31, 2026. The contribution phase runs Oct 5 – Nov 2, 2026 (final applications due Nov 2, 2026). The May–Aug cohort opens in February.
target_persona: Underrepresented students in tech looking for a structured, mentored paid entry point into open source.

title: The Thiel Fellowship
description: Two-year fellowship awarding $100,000 to young builders aged 22 or younger who pause or skip college to build frontier companies, hardware, or scientific research full-time.
eligibility: Must be 22 years old or younger and willing to leave or pause formal university studies for 2 years.
stipend: $100,000 USD non-dilutive grant over 2 years + Thiel Foundation founder network
timeline: Applications accepted year-round on a rolling basis
required_materials: Online application detailing founder background, technical breakthrough or product traction, and 2-year roadmap.
mentor_notes: Genuinely rolling year-round (~20–30 fellows selected per year). Best suited for student founders who already have working deep-tech prototypes or rapid user growth.
target_persona: High-velocity student founders, hardware hackers, and independent researchers.
